stories.h: Lilian Weng leaves Thinking Machines to rejoin OpenAI as head of internal research
stories.s: Her move shifts a prominent AI-safety researcher from a startup environment to OpenAI, potentially reshaping internal safety priorities and intensifying lab talent competition.
b: Left Thinking Machines citing health reasons, sharing a Slack message and an X post
OpenAI confirms she will rejoin and lead a top-level team to accelerate internal research, with cross-research on recursive self-improvement
Previously served as OpenAI's VP of AI Safety Research
Techmeme notes The Information reported she co-founded Thinking Machines Lab and left TML over workload-related health concerns before returning to OpenAI
body: Lilian Weng, co-founder of Thinking Machines, announced this week that she would step down from her role, citing health issues. In a Slack message she shared on X, she wrote, “I don’t feel I’m able to continue at the pace a startup requires,” adding that the amount of consistent stress and workload have pushed her beyond what her health can sustain.

OpenAI said she would rejoin the company, where she previously served as the VP of AI Safety Research. OpenAI’s spokesperson said Weng will lead a top-level team focused on accelerating OpenAI’s internal research, and that the team will support cross-research work on recursive self-improvement.

TechCrunch notes that the move could be read as contradictory to Weng’s statements about the impact of working at a fast-paced startup on her health, though she is unlikely to face as much direct pressure while working at a bigger company.

Mira Murati responded to Weng’s X post with support for her decision to focus on her health, writing, “It is a hard and sad decision. I shared this message with folks at Thinky. Thank you all for the time together♥️ Just as the last sentence in my message: The future worth building is human.”

Techmeme’s coverage cites The Information reporting that Weng is returning to OpenAI after announcing earlier this week she was leaving Thinking Machines Lab over workload-related health concerns (Lilian Weng, a researcher who cofounded AI startup Thinking Machines Lab alongside former OpenAI Chief Technology Officer Mira Murati)
srcTitles: Thinking Machines co-founder Lilian Weng left the company citing health reasons, then joined OpenAI

stories.h: Google launches Lyria 3.5 in Flow Music with better musicality, lyrics, and vocals
stories.s: For music creators, Lyria 3.5 promises more realistic vocals and lyrics with greater creative control inside Flow Music, potentially changing how AI-assisted tracks are produced
b: Lyria 3.5 delivers significant advancements across musicality, lyrics, and vocal quality
It rolls out today in Google Flow Music
The update emphasizes enhanced creative control for users
body: According to blog.google, Lyria 3.5 delivers significant advancements across musicality, lyrics, and vocal quality and is rolling out today in Google Flow Music.
The post says Lyria 3.5 is designed to help users craft richer tracks with greater creative control.
Google describes the update as part of Flow Music's ongoing effort to bring more capable AI music tools into creator workflows.
The blog notes that users will be able to produce songs they love with the improved vocal realism and lyric detail provided by Lyria 3.5.

stories.h: OpenAI offers free access to its most advanced ChatGPT models for 100,000 academic researchers
stories.s: Giving 100,000 researchers free access to advanced AI models could speed up scientific analysis, widen collaboration across institutions, and democratize access to powerful tools.
b: 100,000 academic researchers
free access to ChatGPT's most advanced AI models

body: OpenAI said it is giving 100,000 academic researchers free access to its most advanced ChatGPT models to accelerate scientific research, collaboration, and discovery.
The program is described as broad in scope, targeting researchers across fields with the goal of speeding up experimentation and data analysis using the company’s AI tools.
The release frames the effort as a strategic move to expand access to powerful AI for research, aiming to accelerate discovery and cross-institution collaboration.
srcTitles: Accelerating scientific discovery with ChatGPT for Academic Researchers
